required_outcomes: Moves the oven on: the settings did not help, so it asks the landlord to approve an appliance repair engineer (or sends the approved job to provider selection), rather than repeating the settings advice.

Gives the fence and the bathroom extractor fan their own requests (or records each for separate handling with the right trade: fencing or garden, and electrical), not added to the oven job or the appliance engineer's instruction.
Replies to the tenant covering all three items: what happens next for the oven, and that the fence and the fan have been logged separately, without inventing dates or contractors.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the landlord about all three items in one message, provided each item has its own decision and the oven approval does not stand in for the others.
Asking the tenant for photos of the fence and confirmation that the bathroom has a window, before raising those two with the landlord, provided they are recorded.
positive_behaviours: Suggests opening the bathroom window after showers while the extractor is off, to limit condensation and mould.
Asks whether the leaning fence panel is a risk to anyone using the garden.
red_flags: Answering only the oven and silently dropping the fence or the extractor fan.
Escalating routine items to a human.
prohibited_actions: Asking the appliance repair engineer to look at the fence or the bathroom fan.
Approving spend on any of the three items without the landlord's approval or a spend limit on record.
critical_failures: Losing the fence or the extractor fan: neither recorded nor mentioned to the tenant.
